title: Exit Codes in Python
description: An interpreter should call sys.exit with a meaningful code before it terminates: 0 for success, non-zero for failure.

steps.description: This imports `sys` and defines `main`. The comment marks where the interpreter runs, before it decides on an exit code.
When an error occurred, `sys.exit(1)` exits with a non-zero code, which means failure. Otherwise `sys.exit(0)` exits with zero, which means success.

steps.question: The page says the shell, CI systems, and your test harness all read the exit code. What does exit code `0` mean?
